the cause, measured, and how I fix it

REPRODUCED ON YOUR LIVE PLANNER
Built a repeating branch called Activities with two children, cleared its Due Date and pressed Save. The warning fires.
The cause, measured. I asked the guard directly, with the date and without it:
with a date  → "must be a routine or a habit"
no date    → "must be a routine or a habit"
Clearing the date cannot escape it — the message does not depend on the date at all. The rule only accepts an item that sits under Habits or Routines:
hostIds = { '__habits': 1, '__routines': 1 }
isHost(n) → title is "habits" or "routines", or n.__hr
anything else, including a branch → the warning
That is also why setting Location to the branch does not help, which you found: "Activities" is a branch, not one of those two hosts. A branch is simply not allowed to repeat.

The picture shows: the same Edit window on the same branch, Due Date cleared and saved in both.

I also thought of — you have not decided this yet

Parked, as you asked — but two things are worth deciding before I touch it.

  • Should a branch be allowed to repeat at all? The rule exists for a reason: a repeating item needs somewhere to come back to, and Habits / Routines is where the planner keeps those. If a branch can repeat, I need to know what "tomorrow’s copy" of a branch means — does it bring its children?
  • Or should the warning simply not fire when you are REMOVING the date? That is the narrower fix and matches what you were trying to do: take it off the calendar and leave it in the tree. It would not let a branch repeat, but it would stop blocking you from putting one back.
I would take the second unless you tell me otherwise — it solves the thing you hit without changing what a repeat means.
